ARC Raiders is a glaring example of how a game can collapse under its own incompetence. The title is built on so many fundamentally flawed systems that calling it unfinished would be generous.

The foundational mechanics are a mess. Movement is so poorly implemented that you can’t even step on rocks without being thrown halfway down a mountain. Basic traversal - something modern games mastered a decade ago - is somehow completely broken here. The fact that you can’t even vault over a pebble tells you everything you need to know about the level of polish.

Despite an entire catalogue of weapons, the reality is that only 2-3 weapons are actually reliable and used by 98% of players, and grenades are so broken that they dominate fights with zero counterplay. They’re overtuned and completely out of alignment with the rest of the combat. Everything else is either underpowered, inconsistent, or so clunky that it’s effectively useless. This forces every player into the same boring, predictable meta because the game simply doesn’t function well enough to support variety.

Rocketeers are hilariously overtuned - they fire missiles that can practically not be dodged, no matter how early you react or how far you run. It’s almost comedic at this point: “Here, survive this unfair flying weaponized vaccum cleaner while your character gets stuck on a pebble”.

Meanwhile, Wasps and Hornets aren’t obstacles, threats, or meaningful enemies. They’re just there to disrupt gameplay and waste your time. They add nothing to the experience except frustration, like little flying reminders that quality control didn’t make it to launch.

The PvP is, without exaggeration, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There is no strategic depth, no meaningful balancing, and no sense that encounters are determined by anything other than luck, who shoots first, and poor netcode. Matchmaking is just as incompetent: queue as a duo, and you’ll almost always end up against trios, as if balance was never even a consideration. Instead of enhancing the experience, PvP feels like an unwanted bolt-on feature that makes the rest of the game worse.

Level design is equally awful. The game is riddled with bugs, and the developers don’t even seem remotely interested in fixing them. The terrain works against the player at every turn and collisions are unreliable. Whether you’re climbing, moving, or engaging enemies, the environment is an obstacle in the worst possible way - and not because it’s challenging, but because it’s broken.

The community ends up toxic not because players are inherently bad, but because the game creates an environment where frustration is the default state. When every system is flawed and every encounter is unpredictable for all the wrong reasons, conflict between players becomes unavoidable. And while I’m not a snowflake, the sheer number of times I’ve had to listen to people scream the n-word at me or unleash the most hateful, bigoted, and dehumanizing insults imaginable is absurd. This isn’t trash-talk and it isn’t competitiveness - it’s outright harassment.

These issues are only a fraction of the MANY MANY MANY things wrong with this game. ARC Raiders isn’t just flawed; it’s structurally unsound. Until its core mechanics, systems, and design philosophy are rebuilt from the ground up, and the community finally gets a grip, the experience will remain profoundly disappointing and fundamentally broken. I can’t wait for the glazing period to be over so others can finally see just how bad this game really is.

So it's like Fortnite but with extra hassle of loot management and unoptimized UI.  
Inventory management in this game outside of combat is unnecessarily cumbersome.

1.) Every time you die, you have to RECRAFT everything you need for the next run, This wouldn't be a hassle if you didn't have to jump to 10 different windows every damn time (recraft; weapons, (4x)weapon-attachments, ammo, bandage, shield charger, grenades, utilities)  
Worse: every time you craft one of those said items, you have to dig for them in your massive inventory, and since  your inventory isn't sorted from newest-oldest, it's very tedious.  
2.) When you want to upgrade your equipped gun, for some reason when you click upgrade on it while it's equipped, a different gun is put on your window, you now have to dig in your inventory re-look for the gun you wanted to upgrade.
3.) (Grenades, bandages, Shield rechargers & Gadgets) are all mixed together in the Utility section making it hard to look for your shield-rechargers everytime you craft them. 

For a game with excellent graphics, phenomenal sound design, and amazingly smooth movement, you’d expect the inventory system to be just as polished, but instead, it’s a major disappointment.
10/10 if you want to upset PvE Unc-Millenial retirement home gamers, but otherwise a pretty unremarkable cash in on the extraction shooter genre.
